leading_positions.synthesis: Seven of eleven round 1 files prefer a single-part prize on B001 for Elhanan Helpman and Gene M. Grossman, with the same two laureates in every file. Shared ground: the protection-for-sale framework made lobbying and tariff formation a tractable, testable model; the two-name attribution is described as the cleanest on the shortlist; the core work is about thirty years old. All seven also name the same main weakness, namely mixed and specification-sensitive empirical support for the protection-for-sale predictions, and they differ on how much weight it carries. Not shared: the citation. Andersson, Enflo, Fredriksson and Hassler anchor it narrowly on the political economy of trade policy. Friberg, Strömberg and Teorell also name the innovation-growth-trade strand. Fredriksson, Enflo and Krusell (who is not a supporter) warn that the growth strand goes beyond the ballot's stated discovery and may overlap with the 2025 prize. Those overlap claims come from the files and are not independently verified. Helpman's separate credit on B030 is acknowledged by most supporters, who treat it as a separate contribution. Several supporters list B050, B018, B002 or B036 as alternatives. Alternatives are not votes. Of the four non-supporters, Boppart, Dreber, Hjalmarsson and Krusell each list B001 among their alternatives. The chair is one of the seven supporters.

Hjalmarsson prefers B018 for Autor, Dorn and Hanson, citing new data, credible designs, a conceptual framework, a large follow-on literature and policy influence. She moved from Katz to Dorn in round 1 and now words the citation around technology and trade shocks to labour demand, so it does not claim priority for the task framework. Other members rank B018 highly in the opening (Teorell, Boppart, Enflo and Friberg ranked it second or third) and several list it as an alternative, but no one else prefers it in round 1. Critics point to the unstable third-name cut (Katz versus Dorn), task-framework antecedents outside the credited names, and live debate on shift-share identification and persistence. Hjalmarsson treats that debate as evidence of maturity, not weakness.

Krusell prefers B002 for Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn, on the grounds that random-coefficients demand estimation and dynamic industry models changed empirical industrial organisation and are routine in merger review, antitrust and regulation. He now calls B001 a close alternative and says the two cases differ in kind (method versus theoretical framework). Others (Enflo, Friberg, Strömberg) list B002 as an alternative or rank it second or third. The recurring reservations are the seven-name credit list under a three-name cap (Bresnahan and Reiss left out; Pakes's dynamic-games work partly separate) and whether a methods contribution should count as a discovery.

Boppart prefers B003 for Obstfeld and Rogoff, as founders of the intertemporal, microfounded approach to open-economy macroeconomics. He would draft the citation on the framework first and the exchange-rate puzzles second. He accepts that the puzzles are an unresolved agenda with several originators and that the Redux price-setting assumptions have limited empirical support. Andersson lists B003 as an alternative and Friberg and Strömberg ranked it fourth, but no one else prefers it in round 1.

Dreber prefers B030 for Melitz and Helpman, on the grounds that firm heterogeneity and selection reorganised trade theory and firm-level empirical work and have been heavily tested over two decades. She prefers it to B001 because it rests on denser empirical confrontation. She names the omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum as the main weakness and calls the contribution centred on one landmark paper. B001 supporters cite the same attribution gap as their reason for ranking B030 lower. They treat B001 and B030 as distinct contributions by Helpman and as alternative framings of a trade prize, not additive ones.

areas_of_agreement: All eleven files prefer a single-part configuration; no member proposes combining ballots, and B001 supporters explicitly reject merging B001 with B030.

Every B001 supporter, and several others, describe Grossman-Helpman attribution as clean and the work as mature, while also naming mixed empirical support for protection-for-sale as the main reservation.
Members across fields say they weigh candidates on attribution, maturity and durable influence, and state that opening support counts are not evidence of merit.
Most members distinguish the value of a framework from the empirical fit of one specification, and several say a citation should avoid overclaiming empirical validation.
Members agree that B002, B018, B030 and B003 are serious candidates with real scientific strength, and that their weaknesses lie mainly in attribution, framing or maturity rather than importance.
Members agree the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum omission is a real gap in B030, and that the three-name cap forces hard choices in B002 and B018.
scientific_disputes: How much the mixed and specification-sensitive empirical record of protection-for-sale should count against B001. Supporters see a productive, testable framework; Krusell finds the record more worrying, and Dreber treats it as a reason to prefer B030.

Whether a methods contribution (B002) or a theoretical framework (B001) is the better kind of discovery. Several members say a toolkit prize is not lesser, but ask whether it identifies a single discovery about economic behaviour.
For B018, whether the credibility of the design-based evidence outweighs open debate on shift-share identification and the long-run size and persistence of the China-shock effects.
For B003, whether the intertemporal framework is a distinct discovery or an extension of Mundell-Fleming, and how much the unresolved puzzles and Redux sticky-price assumptions should count.
For B030, whether Melitz's contribution is broad enough for a prize, given its heavy reliance on one 2003 paper, or needs the wider Helpman programme.
Whether B001's distinctness from Krugman's 2008 prize and the 2025 innovation-and-growth prize is sufficient. This is raised in the files but not independently checked here.
attribution_disputes: B001 citation scope: whether the award names only the political economy of trade protection or also trade, innovation and growth. The laureates are the same, but the citation differs among supporters (narrow: Andersson, Enflo, Fredriksson, Hassler; broader: Friberg, Strömberg, Teorell).
Helpman is credited on both B001 and B030. Members disagree on whether this makes the two ballots competing framings of a trade prize or separate achievements.
B030: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum established the exporter facts and parallel models and are not credited; Redding enters later.

B018: the third laureate (Dorn in Hjalmarsson's round 1 proposal and most opening proposals, Katz in her opening) and whether the trade-shock and skill-demand strands are one discovery or two. Task-framework antecedents (Levy and Murnane, Acemoglu and Restrepo) are not credited.

B002: seven credited names against a three-name cap. Bresnahan and Reiss are excluded from the BLP triple, and Pakes's dynamic-games work (Ericson-Pakes, Benkard) is partly separate from the demand framework.
B003: the framework is attributed to Obstfeld and Rogoff, but the puzzles have additional originators (named in the files as Sachs, Svensson, Corsetti and Gopinath).
maturity_disputes: B001, B002 and B003 core work is about thirty years old and is not disputed on maturity; the live questions concern attribution and empirical standing, not time elapsed.

B018: the China-shock evidence dates from about 2013 onward. Hjalmarsson treats a decade of replication and re-estimation as maturity. Andersson, Fredriksson, Hassler, Strömberg and Teorell say persistence and identification debates argue for waiting for consolidation, with some open to it in a later year.
B030: about two decades of testing is generally accepted, and the dispute is about credit, not maturity.
B017 (not preferred by anyone in round 1): Dreber ranked it second but says it is still recent and that independent replication of place-effect estimates is developing.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Chair disclosure: John Hassler is one of the seven explicit B001 supporters. His profile documents no collaboration with Grossman or Helpman. His co-authors include committee members Krusell (B002 supporter), Boppart (B003) and Friberg (B001); none is credited on B001.

Friberg discloses co-authorship with Hassler and Ellingsen and a Chicago Booth co-author (Syverson), none credited on B001. He also notes that IO and trade are his field and that he is married to a former Swedish prime minister, which he says has no apparent bearing on any shortlisted candidate.

Boppart discloses Peter Klenow (credited on B037) as a long-running co-author. B037 is not in his proposal. He also discloses co-authorship with Philippe Aghion and his IIES ties to Hassler and Krusell.
Teorell discloses a co-authored paper with Torsten Persson and a Stockholm University link; this bears on B036, his alternative, not on his B001 preference.
Hassler's opening noted a possible institutional link to Persson at IIES on B036 (his alternative). His profile does not document it.
Dreber discloses Harvard-based positions from 2006 to 2017 as a general institutional overlap only, not a personal tie to any candidate.

Field proximity is disclosed without any recusal claim: Hjalmarsson and Fredriksson for B018 and B017, Krusell for B002 methods, Friberg for B002 and B030, and Strömberg's Chicago Booth adjunct role. Conflicts are disclosed here and not adjudicated.
questions_for_round2: B001 supporters: should the citation be confined to the political economy of trade policy, or should it also name innovation, growth and trade? If the growth strand is included, what does it add that does not rely on the 2025 prize or Krugman's 2008 prize?

What would each non-supporter of B001 (Boppart, Dreber, Hjalmarsson, Krusell) need to see to move it into a first-choice position? Is mixed empirical support for protection-for-sale a disqualifying limit or a normal feature of a productive framework?

On the two trade ballots, can members agree a rule for handling Helpman's credit on both B001 and B030? Can the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum gap in B030 be resolved within a three-name citation, and does it change any member's view?

B018: is the contribution one discovery or two? If the citation is confined to the trade-shock evidence, would members who rank B018 lower (Andersson, Fredriksson, Hassler, Krusell) reconsider, and is Autor-Dorn-Hanson a stable three-name set?

B002: what is the common standard for a methods contribution versus a discovery, and does the BLP triple (Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn) survive the exclusion of Bresnahan and Reiss? Should the chair or secretary check how much of the case rests on Pakes's dynamic-games work?
B003: should a citation rest on the intertemporal framework alone, leaving the exchange-rate puzzles as context? Is the framework distinct from the Mundell-Fleming tradition?

Six members (Andersson, Dreber, Fredriksson, Hassler, Hjalmarsson, Krusell) list B050 among their alternatives, but no one prefers it. What would make B050 a first choice, and does the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises affect its standing?

If B036 (or any ballot with a disclosed link) is pursued in round 2, should the Committee discuss how the disclosed Persson links (Hassler, Teorell) are handled, or continue to treat them as disclosures only?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows one position with explicit multi-member support and four single-member positions. Seven files prefer B001 for Helpman and Grossman, all with the same laureates. Four other members prefer B018, B002, B003 and B030 respectively, and each of those four lists B001 among its alternatives. These are stated preferences, not final votes, and no hidden support is inferred. B001 supporters also share the same main reservation, so round 2 turns less on whether the empirical record is mixed than on how much it matters. Open points are the citation scope, the Helpman overlap with B030, the attribution gaps in the alternatives, and the maturity questions on B018. Statements about earlier prizes and external literatures are as reported in the files and have not been independently verified. The chair is one of the B001 supporters, and this summary is a process record, not a ruling.
